subject: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@stellarops.com>, Dana Liu <dana@stellarops.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook

Hi Alex / Dana —

Thanks again for kicking off the onboarding. Attached is the Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix and an operational playbook we plan to run during the initial benchmarking window (links and attachments below). Goal for Sprint Zero: confirm baseline tail-latency and throughput for the chat inference route and validate KV/prefix caching behavior under representative traffic.

Quick highlights:
- Acceptance targets (P95 tokens completion latency) and throughput buckets are in the spreadsheet. The two rows you should focus on are `dev-integration` (early verification) and `prod-smoke` (pre-cutover).
- We plan a two-stage load run: synthetic ramp (k6 scripts) followed by production-like replay (sanitized traces).
- Primary success criteria: P95 <= 320ms for 1k-token median prompts at 50 RPS and 99th percentile degradation under ramp <2x relative to baseline.
- Data handling: no customer prompts are retained beyond test window. We will use scoped redact rules.

Proposed timeline (flexible):
1) Wed Apr 25 — synthetic smoke run (30 minutes)
2) Thu Apr 26 — replay run (60 minutes, lower burst)
3) Fri Apr 27 — combined validation & readout (30 min)

Please confirm the ETA that works for you and whether the replay artifacts you promised last week will be ready. If you'd prefer, we can also have LoadLab run the synthetic stage to reduce coordination overhead.

Attachments: sprint-zero-load-matrix.xlsx (matrix + thresholds), sprint-zero-playbook.pdf (runbook), k6-synthetic-scripts.tar.gz (scripts)

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Redwood Inference | Make inference predictable and economical
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@stellarops.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dana Liu <dana@stellarops.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook

Priya —

Thanks for the doc. Quick responses:
- ETA: We can provide the sanitized replay traces by EOD Wed (Apr 25). Dana will shepherd that.
- Targets: the P95 goal looks aggressive but reasonable. One ask — can we include a secondary acceptance check for tokenization differences? Our prompts have a mix of long code blocks and short instructions; tokenization variance can affect latency.
- Tooling: happy for LoadLab to run synthetic stage, but we want to run the replay from an internal host to ensure network path parity.

Two scheduling notes:
1) If synthetic run is Wed morning, we'll need a 2-hour window to stage the replay artifacts and confirm ops hooks.
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood's warm-start cache will persist between synthetic and replay runs? If not, we should add a cache-warm step.

Appreciate the clear steps — looking forward to the readout.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Staff Engineer, StellarOps
alex.rivera@stellarops.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@stellarops.com>, Dana Liu <dana@stellarops.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, LoadLab Eng <eng@loadlab.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook

Alex — thanks. Short answers inline, plus a few clarifications and the runbook steps we will execute.

- Tokenization variance: agreed — we've added a tokenization-bucket column in the matrix. We'll capture P50/P95/P99 by token-bucket (short/medium/long). See `sprint-zero-load-matrix.xlsx` sheet `tokenization-buckets`.
- Cache persistence: Redwood's warm KV cache is per-node and will be preserved for the follow-up run *only* if we keep the same serving pool. For safety we've added an explicit `cache-warm` task in the playbook — step 2a. If you want persistent warm cache across days we can reserve a short Dedicated pool for the window.
- Replay host: fine to run replay from your host. We'll coordinate IP allowlist and CORS.

Runbook excerpt (attached playbook contains the full checklist):
1) Preflight (10m): confirm model version pinned, route configured, token limits set.
2) Cache-warm (15m): replay a 5–10 minute sample to populate KV prefix and shared caches.
3) Synthetic ramp (30m): k6 ramp 0->100RPS in stair steps; capture detailed traces.
4) Replay run (60m): production-like traffic replay from StellarOps host.
5) Readout (30m): share dashboards, artifacts, and acceptance signoff.

LoadLab: can you confirm you'll run the synthetic stage at 09:00 PDT? If so we'll hold stewarding duties for the replay.

Attachments reiterated. Links to dashboards will be provided in the readout email.

Thanks —
Priya
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@stellarops.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook

Adding a couple infra notes from our side:

- Pool sizing: for the combined synthetic + replay window we'll stage a 4-GPU pool with autoscale disabled to keep latency stable. That will match the expected production CPU/GPU mix you described (g4dn-like).
- Network path: if StellarOps runs replay from their host, please send source IPs to network-ops@redwood.ai; we'll add allowlist rules and preserve port mappings.
- Observability hooks: Marissa will enable token-level cost tracing during the runs and dump traces to the shared drive. Expect a raw traces tar.gz (~200MB) after the replay.

If we see tail-latency bump >2x during the replay, plan B is to pause replay, collect the hot keys via KV dump, then re-run with a warm cache and reduced concurrency.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@stellarops.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, LoadLab Eng <eng@loadlab.io>, Dana Liu <dana@stellarops.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Zero Load Acceptance Matrix & Playbook

All — quick post-run summary and artifacts link. High level: synthetic run (Wed) and replay (Thu) completed. Outcomes:
- P95 for the target 1k-token median prompts at 50 RPS: 305ms (passes acceptance matrix).
- Observed P99 spike during one burst: 980ms; investigation shows a hot-key scrape on a shared KV prefix.
- Replay traces (sanitized) and k6 raw output uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3SprintZero.

Suggested follow-ups:
1) Ben / Redwood infra — can you confirm that the hot-key mitigation we discussed (prefix sharding for that KV namespace) is feasible for production traffic?
2) Priya / CS — we'll plan the formal acceptance signoff meeting next Tue to review results and confirm cutover window.

Thanks to the team and LoadLab. The artifacts are in the Drive link above. We'll attach the replay trace tar.gz once Dana finishes final redaction.

—Alex
